A Walworth County, Wisconsin tax deed sale happens when the county takes ownership of a property because the owner did not pay real estate taxes. The county uses a court process called In Rem foreclosure to get the title. After that, Walworth County sells the property to the public, often through an online auction. This guide breaks down each step and shows you where to check for current listings.

What Is a Tax Deed?

When a property owner does not pay real estate taxes, the debt becomes delinquent. If the taxes stay unpaid long enough, the county can take legal title to the property. This is called a tax deed. The county then sells these properties to the public to recover the unpaid taxes.

What Is a Tax Deed in Walworth County?

When a property owner stops paying real estate taxes in Walworth County, the debt keeps growing. If the owner never pays it back, the county can take the property through a court action known as In Rem foreclosure. Once a judge approves this, Walworth County becomes the full legal owner of the parcel. Only then does the county sell it to a new buyer.

Wisconsin does not sell tax lien certificates. There is no outside investor buying debt and waiting for interest payments. The Walworth County Treasurer’s Office handles delinquent tax collection, and the county itself ends up owning any property it forecloses on before reselling it.

Key Takeaways

  • Walworth County conducts tax deed sales when property owners fail to pay real estate taxes, using In Rem foreclosure.
  • The county Treasurer’s Office manages the process and sells properties via Wisconsin Surplus in online auctions.
  • To bid, monitor the Treasurer’s In Rem Tax Foreclosures page and research the property before placing bids.
  • Buyers must understand properties sell as is, so they should investigate tax histories and potential liens before bidding.
  • Currently, Walworth County has no properties for sale, but listings can change as new foreclosures occur.

Who Runs the Sale?

The Walworth County Treasurer’s Office manages the In Rem foreclosure process. Once the county owns a batch of foreclosed parcels, the Finance Committee decides to sell them under Wisconsin Statute Section 75.69. Past sales have run through Wisconsin Surplus, an online auction company that also handles sales for other Wisconsin counties.

How the Walworth County Tax Deed Process Works

As of now, Walworth County’s Treasurer page shows no county-owned property for sale at this time. This means the county does not have an active batch of foreclosed parcels listed for auction right now. Check the Treasurer’s In Rem Tax Foreclosures page often, since new sales can open once a fresh batch of properties clears foreclosure.

How to Bid on a Walworth County Tax Deed Property

Follow these steps once a sale window opens.

  1. Watch the Treasurer’s In Rem Tax Foreclosures page.

    This is where Walworth County posts sale announcements and links to the auction.

  2. Check Wisconsin Surplus.

    When a sale is active, the county’s auction listings appear on this site. Create a free account so you can bid when the time comes.

  3. Research the parcel.

    Use the county’s Real Estate Tax Parcel Search and GIS mapping tools to check tax history, ownership, and location before you bid.

  4. Pull deed and lien records.

    Contact the Walworth Register of Deeds to look for old claims that might still attach to the property.

  5. Confirm zoning.

    Reach out to the local town, village, or city where the parcel sits to check what the land can legally be used for.

  6. Place your bid.

    Follow the bidding rules and deadlines listed with the specific Wisconsin Surplus auction.

  7. Pay and record your deed

    Once payment clears, record the new deed with the Register of Deeds.

Why Buyers Should Slow Down and Check Everything

Tax deed properties sell as is. Walworth County makes no promises about the condition of any building, and old problems like liens or code issues can still be tied to the land. Before you bid, take these steps:

  • Look up the parcel on the county’s Real Estate Tax Parcel Search for tax and ownership history.
  • Search Register of Deeds records for old liens or unresolved claims.
  • Drive by the property if you can. Interior access is rarely offered.
  • Call the local zoning office to confirm allowed use.
  • Set aside extra money for repairs, cleanup, or back fees.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Walworth County, Wisconsin tax deed?

It is the ownership title the county gets after winning an In Rem foreclosure case against a property with unpaid taxes. The county then sells the property to the public.

Does Walworth County sell tax lien certificates?

No. Like other Wisconsin counties, Walworth County does not sell liens. It takes full title through the court process, then sells the property itself.

Is there a tax deed sale happening right now?

Not at this time. The Treasurer’s page shows no county-owned property listed for sale. Check the page often since this can change once a new batch clears foreclosure.

Where can I find current auction listings when a sale is active?

Walworth County has used Wisconsin Surplus for past online auctions. Watch the Treasurer’s In Rem Tax Foreclosures page for links and dates.

Can I get the property back before the county finishes taking the deed?

The In Rem process allows time for an owner to resolve the tax debt before the court grants judgment. Once judgment is entered and the county takes title, that chance closes.
